hypothesis: Exact exchange-mark paths may reverse the prior L2-midpoint conclusion and support a lower 25, 40, or 60 bps activation profit lock for SP500 breakout-pressure lifecycles.
decision: Exact sampled exchange-mark paths confirm rejection of the 25/15/10 and 40/15/20 activation-floor-giveback policies: both remain negative after modeled costs in chronological validation, with profit factor below 1 and negative net after removing the largest winner. Continue to withhold 60/15/30 because its positive validation result is contradicted by negative development economics and negative development largest-winner sensitivity. Keep the active 100/40/80 SP500 exit contract unchanged. This result rejects only the three tested lower locks and does not establish that the active contract is optimal.
falsifier: Revisit this disposition if the exact source hashes or selected lifecycle identities do not reproduce, if funding and realistic incremental exit slippage reverse the chronological results, or if a preregistered profile-matched policy produces positive after-cost net, profit factor above 1, and positive net excluding its largest winner in both development and untouched forward validation. Exact prospective v3 lifecycles could also update transfer confidence because the historical lifecycle set predates the active v3 route contract.
limitations: Sampled exchange marks cannot reconstruct movement inside each sampling interval.
Counterfactual economics include the source lifecycle fee contract but exclude funding and additional exit slippage.
Four of 35 selected lifecycles are withheld at the primary 15-second completeness threshold rather than imputed.
The lifecycle set belongs to the older v1 provider contract; it is mechanism evidence rather than direct validation of the active v3 route.
Confidence is medium-high only for rejecting or withholding the three tested lower locks; confidence that the active 100/40/80 contract is globally optimal remains low.
Development and validation are already opened historical partitions and are not a new prospective live test.
The three policies were predeclared, but the test does not cover every possible profit-management rule.
This revision is report-only and cannot route, size, enter, close, restart, pause, or promote a strategy.
